title: Scale step smoothing trials — regional GPU autoscaler experiments
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet summarizes the July 2026 experimental sweep on autoscaler step sizes and smoothing windows across the GPU fleet. Goal: find a pragmatic default that reduces kinetic oscillation (churn) and cold-start cost while meeting 99th percentile latency SLOs for hosted inference in US-W and EU-C regions. This doc captures design hypotheses, test matrix, synthetic and replay workloads, key metrics, qualitative observations, and recommended policy changes plus a short runbook update.

Background / motivation:
- Recent incidents in May/June showed repeated scale-out/scale-in cycles in high-variance workloads (chat bursts + background batch embeddings).
- Current min/max + instantaneous-add triggers perform well for steady throughput but cause oscillation for spiky, bursty request patterns.
- We need a policy that: 1) preserves tail latency targets, 2) reduces unnecessary GPU churn (boot/cold cost), 3) keeps per-region headroom predictable for enterprise customers on Dedicated.

Hypotheses tested:
1) Smaller scale steps with exponential smoothing on observed queue pressure reduce overshoot and downstream cache invalidation without materially increasing tail latency.
2) Larger scale steps with longer cooldown windows are better for long multi-minute ramps (sustained growth), but worse for sub-60s burts.
3) Region-specific defaults (US-W vs EU-C) are justified because spot capacity variability and cold-start durations differ by region/provider.

Test matrix (high level):
- Parameters varied: scale_step (1, 2, 4 GPUs), smoothing_alpha (0.2, 0.5, 0.8), cooldown_seconds (30, 120, 300), min_headroom_percent (10%, 25%, 40%), max_provision_delta_per_minute (1, 2, 4 GPUs/min).
- Regions: US-W (p100-ish profile), EU-C (A100/spot-heavy profile).
- Workloads: (a) chat-burst (10k users simulation, 5–20 rps spikes per minute), (b) embeddings-batch background (steady 1000 concurrent but spiky dispatch windows), (c) mixed-production-replay (real user traffic replayed from 2026-06-12 incident window).
- Runs: each config was simulated (fast sim) + one region-level canary on staging infra for 2h.

Metrics collected:
- 99th & 95th token latency (ms)
- Median latency (ms)
- Cold-start count and average cold-start duration (s)
- GPU churn (number of add/remove events per hour)
- Cost delta estimate (USD/hr relative to baseline)
- Missed requests (request requeues/failures)
- Queue depth distribution and sustained queue time (s)

Key results (summary):
- Best tradeoff observed: scale_step = 2 GPUs, smoothing_alpha = 0.5, cooldown = 120s, min_headroom = 25%.
  - 99th latency increased by <3% vs baseline but cold-start count dropped ~45% in mixed workloads.
  - GPU churn fell ~60% for chat-burst scenario vs baseline instantaneous scaling.
  - Estimated cost delta: +2.0% on steady costs but -9% on incident windows (less repeated boot cost).
- Small step (1 GPU) + light smoothing (alpha=0.8) keeps tail latency lowest but had 30% higher churn and ~6% higher cost due to extra cold starts.
- Large step (4 GPUs) with long cooldown (300s) removed churn almost entirely but introduced transient tail latency spikes in sub-minute bursts (99th up to +18%). Not acceptable for hosted customers.
- Region differences: EU-C cold-starts averaged 1.7x longer (container pull + spot reprovision jitter). EU-C benefited more from larger min_headroom (40%) and slightly longer cooldown (180–240s). US-W preferred lower min_headroom (15–25%).

Observations & qualitative notes:
- Smoothing works best when combined with a short lookback on request variance. We added a simple variance-weight in the estimator and saw better reaction to sustained ramps vs single spikes.
- Rate-limited ramp (max_provision_delta_per_minute) prevents a runaway during synthetic stress tests but must be region-tuned; otherwise we introduce under-provisioning on long ramps.
- Deploy-time tradeoffs: larger min_headroom increases base cost but buys stability for Dedicated customers who expect predictability; we should expose a preset for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- We observed interplay with request-level KV cache warming: scale downs that remove nodes with warm KV caches caused user-visible latency regressions when requests hit cache-miss shortly after scale-in. Keeping a small fraction of old nodes for a short TTL reduces this.

Failure cases noted:
- Very short bursts (<10s) still cause cold-starts regardless of smoothing if no warm capacity exists in region. For these, we recommend targeted reserve micro-pools for latency-critical customers.
- When underlying provider preempts spot nodes, the autoscaler misattributed latency increase to workload and scaled up incorrectly; added a provider-signal filter in the estimator after this run.

Recommendations (concrete):
1) Default policy (Hosted): scale_step=2, smoothing_alpha=0.5, cooldown=120s, min_headroom=25%, max_delta=2 GPUs/min. Rollout phased: staging -> small canary (US-W) -> multi-region rollout over 72h.
2) Dedicated preset: increase min_headroom to 40%, cooldown=180s, and optional static reserve micro-pool (2–4 GPUs depending on region capacity tier).
3) EU-C region override: cooldown=180s, min_headroom=30–40% (tune by sku), because of longer cold-starts.
4) Add TTL-protected stale-node buffer: on scale-in, keep 10% of removed nodes in a warm-standby state for 300s to preserve KV caches.
5) Instrumentation: add a provider_preempt_rate signal to autoscaler estimator and surface it to the console; add an alert when provider_preempt_rate > 2% in 5m.
6) Rollback plan: if 99th latency increases >10% post-rollout in any region for >30m, auto-revert to previous policy and trigger an incident.

Runbook snippet (ops):
- When alert "autoscaler-churn-above-threshold" fires, check last 30m churn and cold-start counts. If cold-starts are driving churn, toggle smoothing_alpha up by 0.1 and increase cooldown by 60s in the policy for the affected region.
- For Dedicated customers complaining about perceived capacity drift, apply the Dedicated preset and communicate expected headroom and cost delta.

Open items / next steps:
- Longitudinal cost study across three months to confirm cost model (quantify savings during repeated incidents).
- Expand the synthetic workload suite to include multi-tenant interference scenarios.
- Product: expose 3 autoscaler presets in Console (Hosted, Dedicated, Low-cost) and document tradeoffs in the admin UX.
- SRE: schedule a chaos run that preempts 5% of nodes during a ramp to validate provider_preempt_rate filter.

Appendix: notable raw numbers (canary runs, US-W staging vs baseline):
- Baseline: churn=12 adds/removes/hr, cold-starts=18/hr, 99th latency=420ms
- Best config: churn=4 adds/removes/hr, cold-starts=10/hr, 99th latency=432ms, cost_delta +2% steady, -9% incident window
- Large-step config: churn=1 adds/removes/hr, cold-starts=4/hr, 99th latency=495ms (unacceptable for hosted)

Contact / owner: Asha Patel (eng-infrastructure). Changes to policy must go through JIRA-7890 and PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/456.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working doc; please add experiment notes inline in the PR above or send quick comments on Slack #infra-autoscaler. We'll freeze defaults for prod after the canary window on 2026-08-02.
